pr.title: Account for immutably borrowed locals in MIR copy-prop and GVN
pr.description:
For the most part, we consider that immutably borrowed `Freeze` locals still fulfill SSA conditions. As the borrow is immutable, any use of the local will have the value given by the single assignment, and there can be no surprise.

This allows copy-prop to merge a non-borrowed local with a borrowed local. We chose to keep copy-classes heads unborrowed, as those may be easier to optimize in later passes.

This also allows to GVN the value behind an immutable borrow. If a SSA local is borrowed, dereferencing that borrow is equivalent to copying the local's value: re-executing the assignment between the borrow and the dereference would be UB.

r? @ghost for perf
pr.author: cjgillot

processing.reason:
The historical rewrite is `opaque::<T>((*_3))` -> `opaque::<T>(_1)` only when `_3` is `Value::Address { kind: AddressKind::Ref(BorrowKind::Shared), place: P }` and `simplify_place_value(P)` succeeds. In the historical code this success is itself gated by `VnState::project`'s `Deref` arm, which returns `None` unless the dereferenced reference is immutable (`Mutability::Not`, i.e. not `&mut`/raw) AND its pointee type is `Freeze`; additionally `SsaLocals::new` demotes any immutably-borrowed local whose type is not `Freeze` to `Set1::Many` (non-SSA), so its value is unknown to GVN. That is exactly why the `gvn.non_freeze` test keeps `opaque::<T>((*_3))` unchanged, and why raw-pointer/`&mut` borrows are never folded.

For the cases the code actually rewrites, `_1` is a Freeze, single-assignment local whose definition dominates the borrow (and hence the dereference). A shared borrow of a Freeze local cannot be used to mutate the local, and `SsaLocals`/GVN require the sole assignment to dominate all uses, so the value of `_1` cannot change between `_3 = &_1` and `*_3`; `*_3` denotes the same place/value as `_1`. The transformed operand even remains a read of the same local place, so no stale-value substitution occurs. Constructing a differing pair therefore requires applying the rewrite outside its actual guard (non-Freeze pointee, `&mut`, or raw address), which is the historical *excluded* case, not the historical transformation. A pair relying on address identity is also outside the allowed evidence (address observations are prohibited). Hence there is no source-grounded concrete input on which the historical original and the historical rewrite produce different defined values; no valid counterexample pair can be encoded.

analysis.summary: GVN may replace a dereference of a shared reference to an SSA local with that local's value (`(*_3)` -> `_1`), but only when the address is `AddressKind::Ref(BorrowKind::Shared)` and the pointee is a Freeze SSA local. Raw pointers, mutable borrows, and non-Freeze pointees must not be simplified.
analysis.originalLogic: Before the PR, `simplify_place_value` walked a place's projections using `try_as_local`/`project` but had no case for `Value::Projection(pointer, ProjectionElem::Deref)` whose pointer value is a `Value::Address`; consequently the MIR kept `_0 = opaque::<u32>((*_3))` even when `_3 = &_1` and `_1` was SSA.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The optimization rewrites a dereference of an immutable borrow into the borrowed local's value, i.e. `opaque::<T>((*_3))` becomes `opaque::<T>(_1)` when `_3 = &_1`. This is only valid for a shared reference to a Freeze SSA local; applying it to `*const`/`*mut`/raw addresses, to `&mut`, or to a non-Freeze pointee is unsound because the memory may be modified between the borrow and the dereference. The `non_freeze` GVN test deliberately leaves `opaque::<T>((*_3))` unchanged.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR with `_2 = _1; _3 = &_1; opaque::<&T>(_3); opaque::<T>(_2); opaque::<T>((*_3))`. The positive variant is `T: Copy + Freeze` (or a concrete `u32`); the negative variants are a generic `T: Copy` with no `Freeze` bound, or a raw/mutable borrow kind.
analysis.trigger: A shared borrow of a single-assignment local is dereferenced after the borrow, and GVN asks whether the dereferenced value equals the local's SSA value.
preconditions: The pointer value is `Value::Address { kind: AddressKind::Ref(BorrowKind::Shared), .. }`.
`simplify_place_value(&mut pointee, location)` succeeds so the pointee resolves to an SSA value.
The pointee local is Freeze/SSA (enforced upstream by `SsaLocals`; non-Freeze locals are `Set1::Many`).
pitfalls: Match only `BorrowKind::Shared`; raw pointers and `&mut` are not covered and must not be folded.
Do not fold `Deref` of an arbitrary pointer value that was loaded from memory; the pointer must itself be a `Value::Address` to a borrow.
Apply the handling both inside the projection loop (`&place.projection[index..]`) and after the loop (empty residual projection), otherwise only partially-projected places are optimized.
Do not rely on type checks only at the GVN site: a non-Freeze local is excluded by being non-SSA, so never bypass `simplify_place_value`/SsaLocals.
analysis.testStrategy: Extend `tests/mir-opt/gvn.rs` with custom_mir `borrowed<T: Copy + Freeze>` and `non_freeze<T: Copy>` doing `let a = x; let r1 = &x; opaque(r1); opaque(a); opaque(*r1);`. CHECK bb1 uses `_1`, bb2 uses `_1` for Freeze, but for non-Freeze bb2 must stay `opaque::<T>((*_3))`. EMIT_MIR for both panic strategies to compare before/after.
evidence: This also allows to GVN the value behind an immutable borrow.
If a SSA local is borrowed, dereferencing that borrow is equivalent to copying the local's value: re-executing the assignment between the borrow and the dereference would be UB.
